_README: The published OSIE row, transcribed by hand from the paper. This is the ONE part of
the F1 run record that cannot be generated: nothing in this repository contains the
paper's numbers -- result-images/main-result.png is qualitative scanpath figures and
the READMEs carry no table -- so they are typed in once, here, with provenance, and
from then on they are data like everything else.
Fill in the values you can read off the paper and LEAVE THE REST null. A null is
reported as '--' meaning UNKNOWN; it is never treated as zero and never as agreement.
Do not guess a number to fill a hole -- a wrong reference silently turns a real
discrepancy into an apparent match, which is the D7 failure mode applied to the
Note on what to transcribe: the paper's OSIE row for the SAME configuration this run
used -- few-shot personalized prediction, 10-shot, the 5 unseen query subjects. A row
for a different shot count or a different subject split is not a comparable number.
source: Xue et al., 'Few-shot Personalized Scanpath Prediction', CVPR 2025 — OSIE block of the n-shot results table, row 'ISP-SENet' at n = 10.
transcribed_by: lulloa (screenshot of the paper's table) — read off by Claude Code and confirmed against the run's num_fewshot=10
notes: ONLY the three composites are transcribed. The OSIE block of that table carries exactly SM / MM / SED, so the per-dimension MultiMatch values, the two ScanMatch variants, STDE and the retrieval block have NO published counterpart there and are deliberately left null — they render as '--' = UNKNOWN, never as agreement. The n = 10 row is the comparable one: this run used --num_fewshot 10 with fewshot_user_embedding_10.pt (the paper's n = 1 and n = 5 rows are different configurations and must not be compared against). SED is lower-is-better; SM and MM are higher-is-better.
